The preexisting wedge homotopy and computed Morse complex agree, but neither alone substitutes for the integral orbit-basis proof.

originality.rationale: The same-object prior exact seven-sphere homotopy calculation has been inspected in full, and specifically does not determine equivariant homology. Jonsson already tabulates the rank seven and studies crosspolytopal cycles on periodic grids; this result adds an exhaustive eight-carrier census, the integral deletion-minor basis and relation, and the full rank-seven integral B4-lattice, none implied by a Betti number or construction of some cycles. Bousquet-Melou et al treat open/cylindrical boundary conditions, and Barmak proves general suspension results. Exact targeted searches found no directly covering statement, with unindexed material a residual risk.
residual_risks: Equivalent specialized unindexed computations may exist; search and limited primary access cannot certify absolute publication priority.

value.rationale: For the smallest fully periodic four-by-four grid/four-dimensional cube, fundamental crosspolytopal sphere cycles are the natural explicit geometric homology representatives. Prior literature explains that cross-cycles need not generate the whole integral homology. Here their exact minimum-support census, any-seven unimodular generation, sole primitive relation, and full integral group module answer that nontrivial representability and symmetry question. The result distinguishes the integral quotient lattice from rational character or rank and is useful for equivariant topology of periodic-grid independence complexes, rather than a rerun of its known Betti number.
